title: [enhancement] Globally activate/deactivate communication with AC
body:
**Use case:** 
A global variable to activate/deactivate the communication of all tapir components with archicad would be nice, just to avoid time taking updates when tweaking some parameter in GH.

**Implementation proposal:**

- Controlled by an input only component. 

- The component should implement a "singleton pattern", so only one copy of the component can exist on the GH canvas.

- For global accessibility, the boolean "activateCommunication" flag should be stored at sticky

- All communication triggering commands should be preceded by  "communicate" flag state check . The checking method will be stored at the module file.

title: New versioning scheme
body:
### Problem

Right now:
- the Archicad Add-On version is `0.1.4`,
- the Python library version is `1.0.0`,
- the Grasshopper plugin version is `0.2.0`.

With these differences it's hard to tell if a component is compatible with another one, so it can quickly become a mess if you don't update all components at the same time.

### Proposal

Unify the version number for all components, let's say `1.0.0` for everything. It means that upon every release all the components must be released. It also means that there must be exactly one file in the repository that specifies the release version, and it must be updated after every release publish.

What do you think?

I tried 3 solutions:
1. Rename 'elements' input parameter to 'elementsWithColors' and that array would contain elementId+color pairs.

title: python scripts by KAA DESIGN
body:
https://github.com/KAA-MB/archicad-python-scripts-KAA

I'd love to help incorporate some of the script logic / features into Tapir in the future!  Here are descriptions of the scripts included:

ZONE NUMBERING BY DISTANCE FROM FIRST
•	Numbers Zones sequentially starting from "First Zone" (a custom property), and proceeding by closest distance from this first zone. If there's a selection, the script uses only selected zones; otherwise it uses all zones in project. Numbering series is unique per story level (e.g. 101, 102 for 1st floor; 201, 202 for 2nd floor).

ZONE NUMBERING BY DISTANCE FROM PREVIOUS
•	Numbers Zones sequentially starting from "First Zone" (a custom property), and proceeding by closest distance from the previous zone numbered. If there's a selection, the script uses only selected zones; otherwise it uses all zones in project. 

ZONE DIMENSIONS
•	Measures each Zone's length and width dimensions (feet-inches) based on Bounding Box, and writes it to a custom property. We use a Zone Label to display these dimensions in plan. The script takes a custom property called "Zone Angle" (user input) in order to calculate the dimensions correctly for rotated zones. We did not find a way to pull the rotation angle automatically, so it defaults to 0 degrees and is filled in by the user if different. The math formula breaks at 45 degrees (a compromise, since to fix this would require another user input). If there's a selection, the script uses only selected zones; otherwise it uses all zones in project. 

ATTRIBUTES - create folders and sort attributes into folders (layers example)
•	Creates attribute folders, and sorts attributes into the folders according to our firm’s naming convention. If folders have already been created, it moves all attributes into a temporary “dummy” folder, removes other folders and proceeds with creating/sorting (then erases dummy folder). Attributes not matching the naming convention are placed in a folder called “Audit Non-compliant”.  *script is broken in AC27 due to changes in JSON commands (need help fixing)

ATTRIBUTES - audit names (layers example)
•	Audits attribute names according to our firm’s naming convention, and prints a list of “non-compliant” attributes. 

INTERIOR DOORS - number sequentially
•	Numbers interior Doors sequentially starting from "First Door” (a custom property), and proceeding by closest distance from this first door. The script relies on correct Classification as Door, and uses the built-in property for Position: Interior. If there's a selection, the script uses only selected doors; otherwise it uses all doors in project. Numbering series is unique per story level (e.g. 101, 102 for 1st floor; 201, 202 for 2nd floor).

INTERIOR DOORS - number by zone
•	Numbers interior Doors based on associated Zone’s number + letter of alphabet (e.g. 101a, 101b). The script uses the built-in property for Position: Interior. If there's a selection, the script uses only selected doors; otherwise it uses all doors in project. Ideally this script would also have logic to move clockwise around each zone so the a, b, c sequence is more logical.

EXTERIOR DOORS/WINDOWS
•	Numbers interior Doors and Windows sequentially starting from "First Door” or “First Window” (a custom property), and proceeding clockwise around the building. The script relies on correct Classification as Door or Window, built-in property Position: Exterior, and also takes several custom properties. The clockwise direction is controlled by custom property “Exterior Side” to identify Top, Right, Bottom, Left position in plan (cardinal directions were more error prone since people get confused. Numbering series is unique per “Story Level” (e.g. 101, 102 for 1st floor; 201, 202 for 2nd floor) - we decided to make this a custom property also in order to have more control over numbering of clerestories, since “z bands” didn’t produce reliable results. The “Building Number” custom property defaults to 1, and if the site has multiple buildings the user can identify unique numbers for each (though the numbering starts at 101 for any building, the building’s number doesn’t become part of door/window’s number). This part of the script breaks right now if Building Numbers are not sequential - needs fixing.

title: Number of Requests sent / undo steps generated per component
body:
I would like to discuss the number of requests a component sends when receiving tree input. As most of you are probably aware, currently, Tapir components send one request per data tree branch. 

This is not only problematic from a performance standpoint, as components that change the state of ArchiCAD generate a separate undo step for each request. As the number of undo steps ArchiCAD keeps is capped at 100, this can easily result in lost data.

Simultaneously flattening inputs into lists, and then rebuilding them from the nodes output to data trees can be done, but is far from trivial, especially if the inputs have different number of elements on the corresponding branches.

I think, that in the long run, Tapir components should only send out one request per component.

One way to achieve this is by setting each input/output to dataTree access and modifying the code in the components.
However, this will result in really complicated components. Most of the code can probably be extracted, but the components will be more complex. IronPython had a helper library for this, I used that to create a SetProperties node that only sends one request. A similar library should be available in C#.

Is there any other way? 
If we can somehow know when the last time our component runs we can build up the request and send it out at the end.
But I could not find an event that corresponds to this, and to count the passes we need access to the trees - and that is what I want to avoid. 

What do you think?

title: `CreateObjects` should not need dimensions
body:
I was about to add an example to the repo and discovered that right now we get an error code back if we try to use `CreateObjects` without specifying dimensions.
That is not good UX and a limitation that should be removed.
This is safe because _all_ library parts have their default values set.
I wanted to place the "Armchair 04 26" in the TestProject.pla. A chair is the best example for a libpart that will absolutely be placed without changing it's dimensions.
More so: This behavior has to be considered bad for reason of violating the coders explicit choice (and possibly breaking logic). With this command it is possible to change values that should not be able to be changed. Imagine an object which comes in only one size, so the programmer chose to `lock "A", "B"` the sizes. Still, this script will happily use the provided sizes nonetheless.

I see two tasks:
- [x] Make `dimensions` and its constituents optional; if they are not provided take the libpart's default value [most important!]
- [ ] if a value is `lock`ed (probably not easy to tell), reject the input

 ---

On a sidenote: I also think that "CreateObjects" is a misnomer because we do not actually _create_ an object, but merely _place_ it. 
I know... nitpicking! 😄

title: JSON Schema inconsistencies
body:
Hello!
I have found a few inconsistencies in the schema while generating models from it. I intend to fix these in the next days/weeks, but wanted to share my notes beforehand. 
I think most problems can be fixed without breaking changes.
*Problem/impact fields are AI-generated, you can skip them for a quick read. Left it in for context*

---

## Category 1: Critical Issues – Name Collisions

### 1.1. Redefined `PropertyType` Enum **\[BREAKING!]**

* **Problem:** The name `PropertyType` is used for two completely different enum concepts:

  1. To describe the category of a property (`StaticBuiltIn`, `DynamicBuiltIn`, `Custom`)
  2. To describe the data type of a property's value (`number`, `integer`, `string`, `boolean`)

* **Impact:** This is a direct name collision, making it impossible for a code generator to create correct models without manual intervention.

* **Recommendation:**

  * Rename the enum with values `["StaticBuiltIn", "DynamicBuiltIn", "Custom"]` to **PropertyCategory**.
  * At this point, leaving the `"propertyType"` key pointing to a **PropertyCategory** is misleading. I think it should be changed (**breaking**).
  
@tlorantfy what do you think? Is there a good way to handle this?

---

### 1.2. Redefined Model Names (`Story`, `Hole`, `Geometry`)

* **Problem:** Several core concepts are defined with different structures under the same name, depending on the context (e.g., the `Hole` for a Slab is different from the `Hole` for a Mesh).

* **Impact:** This leads to the same name collision issue as above, forcing the generation of suffixed models like `Story1`, `Hole1`, `Hole4`, and `Geometry1`. This breaks the ability to use a consistent `Model(**data)` pattern for object creation.

* **Recommendation:** Provide unique and descriptive names for these context-specific definitions:

  * **Story:**

    * `SetStories` and `GetStories` use two different objects, but they share the common `stories` name.
    * Solution: Create two new common schema definitions: **StoryParameters** and **StorySettings**.

  * **Hole:**

    * `Hole` should be a referenced common object in **CommonSchemaDefinitions**.
    * Mesh holes use 3D coordinates instead of 2D. Is that correct?
    * But even if meshes use 2D holes, Roofs should use 3D, I think. If so, the names should be **Holes2D** and **Holes3D**.

  * **Geometry:**

    * Create two new common schema definitions: **ManualZoneGeometry** and **ReferenceZoneGeometry**.

---

## Category 2: Schema Improvements & Consistency

### 3.1. Invalid JSON Schema Type: `double`

* **Problem:** The schema uses `"type": "double"`, which is not a standard JSON Schema type.

* **Impact:** This can cause validation failures with strict JSON Schema tools.

* **Recommendation:** Replace all instances of `"type": "double"` with the correct standard: **`"type": "number"`**.

---

### 3.2. Inconsistent `TypeSpecificDetails` Definition

* **Problem:** `SetDetailsOfElements` and `GetDetailsOfElements` are now developed in parallel, so the two `TypeSpecificDetails` definitions are different.

* **Impact:** This causes the code generator to create a separate, incorrect `TypeSpecificDetails1` model, making the `SetDetailsOfElementsParameters` model less type-safe and harder to use than it should be.

* **Recommendation:** Rename to:

  * **TypeSpecificParameters**
  * **TypeSpecificSettings**

---

### 3.3. Missing Core Definitions for Attribute Properties

* I think it is already fixed? Will need to check.

title: Fix 3D Bounding Box accuracy for Roofs and Zones by excluding drafting elements
body: **Problem:** The standard `ACAPI_Element_CalcBounds` returns the "Model Extent," which includes non-geometric drafting aids. This can result in significantly inflated bounding boxes for **Roofs** (due to pivot lines) and **Zones** (due to 3D text stamps). **Solution:** Implemented a new helper, `CalculateSolidBodyBounds`, which filters out wireframe bodies (`nPgon == 0`) and calculates bounds from the solid geometry only. For roofs and zones we use this function instead of `ACAPI_Element_CalcBounds`. **Reasoning** At first I wanted to add a "calculationMethod" enum to the schema, and let the user decide how to calculate bbs to avoid changes to behaviour. After testing the new function it is clear that this simple implementation while working for the real pain points (zones and roofs, even multi-plane) fails for a number of element types. We would need to implement it on a per elemen-type base, so I opted out of this approach. **Additional thouths** - API_BodyType stores it's bounds in float, API_Box3D stores it in a double. The conversion causes an accuracy issue. I did not round it in the addon, left it for the script user - The new method might be good for objects as well, but relies on the correct use of BODY ENDBODY tags, which I did not use correctly in my gdl objects. Needs further testing, left behaviour unchanged. - ACAPI_Element_CalcBounds behaves wierd on doors / windows. For most doors it only considers the 2d symbol, but for some it considers the 3d as well. title: Fix CreateSlabs level parameter at story boundaries
body:
## Problem

When `CreateSlabs` is called with a `level` value at or above a story boundary, the slab is placed at an incorrect Z position. The level value gets effectively doubled.

**Example** (with Story 1 at 3m):
- `level: 2.9` → slab at z=2.9 ✓
- `level: 3.0` → slab at z=6.0 ✗ (expected 3.0)
- `level: 3.1` → slab at z=6.1 ✗ (expected 3.1)

## Cause

In `CreateSlabsCommand::SetTypeSpecificParameters`, the input level is stored directly in `element.slab.level`, then used to compute the floor index, but never converted to a story-relative offset. Since Archicad interprets `slab.level` as relative to the assigned story, the result is:

```
actual_z = story_level + slab.level = 3.0 + 3.0 = 6.0
```

## Fix

Follow the pattern used by `CreateColumnsCommand` (line 164) and `CreateObjectsCommand` (line 740): store input in a temp variable, then set `element.slab.level` to the computed offset.

```cpp
double inputLevel = 0.0;
parameters.Get ("level", inputLevel);
const auto floorIndexAndOffset = GetFloorIndexAndOffset (inputLevel, stories);
element.header.floorInd = floorIndexAndOffset.first;
element.slab.level = floorIndexAndOffset.second;
```

## Verified

Tested on AC29. All test cases now produce correct Z positions.

When commands receive an invalid or misspelled type parameter, they silently return unexpected results instead of an error.

**Examples:**
- `GetElementsByType(elementType: "wall")` → returns ALL elements (expected: error)
- `GetAttributesByType(attributeType: "surface")` → returns empty/all (expected: error)

- GetFavoritesByType
- GetConnectedElements

title: Lessons learned building a Tapir-based automation toolkit (AC29)
body:
Hi! I've been building a custom Archicad automation toolkit on top of Tapir (AC29, Windows). Along the way I ran into several undocumented behaviors, built some features that might be useful to the broader community, and collected build system gotchas that could save other developers time. Sharing these here in case they're helpful.

---

## API Findings

**1. `elemInfoString` is read-only via `ACAPI_Element_Change`**

Using `APIMemoMask_ElemInfoString` with `ACAPI_Element_Change` silently fails — the write goes through without error, but the value doesn't change. The correct function is `ACAPI_Element_ChangeElementInfoString` (declared in `ACAPI_Database.h`).

**2. `GetConnectedElements` requires per-type queries**

You can't retrieve all connected elements (Windows, Doors, Skylights) in a single call. Each `connectedElementType` must be queried separately. This isn't documented in the command schema.

**3. JS Bridge: nested `JS::Object` returns don't work as JS objects**

When using `RegisterAsynchJSObject` with `DG::Browser`, returning nested `JS::Object` structures doesn't produce usable JavaScript objects. The workaround is to serialize to a JSON string via `JS::Value` and parse with `JSON.parse()` on the JS side. Also: all JS bridge functions return Promises — always use `await`.

**4. HTTP requests to localhost from within an Add-On deadlock**

Calling the Tapir HTTP server from within the same Archicad process (e.g. via an HTTP client in your Add-On) causes a deadlock. The JS bridge callback and the HTTP server share threading resources. Always use direct `ACAPI_*` calls instead.

---

## Features I ended up building (and would love to see in Tapir)

**Layer Management** — Tapir has `CreateLayers` and `CreateLayerCombinations`, but no commands to read, modify, or delete layers. In my project I needed:
- Get/Set the current active layer
- Rename and delete layers
- Move elements between layers in bulk
- Read/write layer intersection groups
- Get element counts per layer

These are probably the most common layer operations in day-to-day BIM automation.

**Classification Import/Export** — Tapir can get and set classifications per element, but there's no way to import or export entire classification systems as XML. This would be useful for transferring classification standards between projects or offices.

---

## Build system gotchas (AC29 + Windows)

A few things that cost me hours and aren't documented anywhere:

| Issue | What happens | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| VS 2022 17.13+ / VS 2026 | `GSRoot/Definitions.hpp` blocks `_MSC_VER >= 1950` | Invoke `vcvarsall.bat x64 -vcvars_ver=14.42` to force v143 toolset |
| `API_Attr_Head.name` | `GS::ucscpy` fails — it's `char[]`, not `uchar_t[]` | Use `strncpy` instead |
| `Support/Lib/` on Windows | `.lib` files aren't included in the standard DevKit unzip | Extract manually from `API.Development.Kit.WIN.29.3000.zip` |
| Ninja build cache | Stale `.obj` files after code changes cause phantom errors | Delete `.obj` files from `CMakeFiles/AddOn.dir/Sources/` |

---

## Happy to contribute

If any of these findings are useful, I'm happy to open individual issues or submit PRs for specific items. Just let me know what format works best for the project.

Thanks for building Tapir — it's a great foundation for Archicad automation.

body:
## Summary

Adds programmatic access to ArchiCAD's libpart inventory and project Favorites database. Builds on closed PR #379's `GetAvailableLibraryParts` idea but re-derived from main, AC29-compatible, with the original review feedback addressed.

### New commands

1. **`GetAvailableLibraryParts(filterByTypeId?)`** — enumerates the loaded libpart inventory. Returns `{guid, index, documentName, fileName, typeId}` per part, plus `skippedCount` + `skippedSample` (first 5 `{index, code}`) when `ACAPI_LibraryPart_Get` fails on individual indices. The `documentName` is the locale-translated name AC displays, which `CreateObjects` accepts as `libraryPartName`.

2. **`ImportFavorites(path, targetFolder?, importFolders?, conflictPolicy?)`** — wraps `ACAPI_Favorite_Import`. Loads a `.prefs` file or folder of Favorites into the current project. `conflictPolicy` is one of `Error`/`Skip`/`Overwrite` (default)/`Append`. On `Error` + name collision, returns `firstConflictName`.

3. **`ExportFavorites(path, names?)`** — wraps `ACAPI_Favorite_Export`. Dumps the project's Favorites database to a file or folder. `names=null` exports all; pass a subset list to filter.

Together with the existing `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults`, these enable the full "good GDL defaults" workflow programmatically: capture once in UI → export to `.prefs` → share/import across projects → apply for headless `CreateDoors`/`CreateWindows`/`CreateObjects`.

### Why this isn't a #379 re-submit

#379 bundled two unrelated features and was closed. This PR ships just `GetAvailableLibraryParts` (door/window libpart spec dropped) + adds the Favorites import/export wrappers. Independent, AC29-compatible, with the review feedback baked in.

## Changes addressing prior review notes

- Memory leak fix: `ACAPI_LibraryPart_Get` allocates `libPart.location`; loop now frees it on every successful Get (was ~7k leaked allocations per call on a stock AC29 library).
- `skippedCount` + `skippedSample` exposed so callers can distinguish "complete inventory" from "partial enumeration".
- AC29 compat: `APILib_*` enum prefix (vs the pre-AC28 `API_*`), `docu_UName` (wide-char) vs `docu_Name`, `GS::UnID(...).GetMainGuid().ToUniString()` for guid conversion.
- `ExportFavorites` response is an empty `GS::ObjectState` rather than `CreateSuccessfulExecutionResult()` (the latter injects `success: true` which `additionalProperties: false` rejects via 4009).
- `ImportFavorites` with `Error` policy: special-cases `APIERR_NAMEALREADYUSED + firstConflictName` so the name reaches the caller (was being swallowed by `CreateErrorResponse`).

## Test plan

Tested live on AC29 trial (build 3000, FRA) after deploy:

- [x] `GetAvailableLibraryParts(filterByTypeId="Object")` returns 3504 Object entries
- [x] `skippedCount=92`, `skippedSample` populated with `{index, code}` pairs
- [x] `ExportFavorites` writes `.prefs` (131KB) for a project with existing Favorites
- [x] `ImportFavorites` round-trips the exported file with `Overwrite` policy → ok
- [x] `ImportFavorites` with `Error` policy hits an existing Favorite → returns `firstConflictName` ("150/300 Blocs d'entrelacement préfabriqués")

Also build-tested for AC28 with ACAPI 28.4001 SDK + v142 toolset (no source changes needed; same enum names).

## Files

- `archicad-addon/Sources/LibraryCommands.cpp` + `.hpp` — `GetAvailableLibraryParts`
- `archicad-addon/Sources/FavoritesCommands.cpp` + `.hpp` — `ImportFavorites` / `ExportFavorites`

title: feat(doors,windows): optional favoriteName for CreateDoors/Windows
body:
## Summary

Adds optional `favoriteName` field to `CreateDoors` and `CreateWindows`. When provided, the named Favorite is applied to the Door/Window tool defaults before element creation. This unblocks creation on a fresh project where the Door/Window tool has never been opened in the UI; otherwise `ACAPI_Element_CreateExt` can reject the cloned defaults with `APIERR_REFUSEDPAR`.

## Two Commits

1. **`feat(doors,windows): support favoriteName for CreateDoors / CreateWindows`** — applies the Favorite before `PrepareWindowOrDoorDefaults`.
   - Calls `ACAPI_Favorite_Get` by name and opts into `elementMarker` / `memoMarker`.
   - Calls `ACAPI_Element_ChangeDefaultsExt` with mask `FULL`, passing the Favorite marker as a Main Marker sub-element when present.
   - Replays classifications, category values, and user-defined properties via `TAPIR_Element_*` helpers.

   Ordering matters: the helper runs before `PrepareWindowOrDoorDefaults` so the marker built from `ACAPI_LibraryPart_GetMarkerParent` matches the favorite-applied libpart. Reverse ordering leaves the outer marker stale and `CreateExt` fails.

2. **`fix(doors,windows): validate favoriteName element type matches command`** — rejects mismatched Favorites. Passing a Window Favorite to `CreateDoors`, or a Door Favorite to `CreateWindows`, returns `APIERR_REFUSEDPAR`.

## Schema

```json
{
  "doorsData": [
    {
      "ownerWallId": { "guid": "..." },
      "centerOffset": 1.0,
      "favoriteName": "Porte d'entrée"
    }
  ]
}
```

`favoriteName` is the Favorite name as returned by `GetFavoritesByType`, not the libpart's `docu_UName`. Existing callers without `favoriteName` keep the current behavior.

## Why

Programmatic Door/Window placement on a freshly-opened project can fail unless the user has opened the corresponding tool in the UI first. This adds a clean way to seed tool defaults through the existing Favorite mechanism.

Companion to the ImportFavorites / ExportFavorites PR (#381), but independent: these commands work on any project that already has the relevant Favorites.

Targets Tapir 1.4.1.

- `CreateWindows` with Door Favorite `Porte d'entrée` is rejected with `APIERR_REFUSEDPAR`.

title: feat(stairs): add CreateStairs command
body:
## Summary

Adds a new `CreateStairs` command that creates Stair elements from a baseline polyline and optional dimensional parameters.

This is a first implementation covering straight and multi-segment stairs (L-shaped, U-shaped). Subelements (risers, treads, structures) are generated automatically by Archicad from the main parameters.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `baseLinePoints` | `Coordinate2D[]` | yes | 2D coordinates defining the stair baseline. Min 2 points. |
| `zCoordinate` | `number` | yes | Absolute elevation of the stair base |
| `totalHeight` | `number` | no | Total height of the stair |
| `flightWidth` | `number` | no | Width of the stair flight |
| `stepNum` | `integer` | no | Number of risers (steps) |
| `riserHeight` | `number` | no | Height of each riser |
| `treadDepth` | `number` | no | Depth (going) of each tread |

## Example

```json
{
  stairsData: [{
    baseLinePoints: [
      {x: 0.0, y: 0.0},
      {x: 3.0, y: 0.0}
    ],
    zCoordinate: 0.0,
    totalHeight: 2.80,
    flightWidth: 1.20,
    stepNum: 16,
    riserHeight: 0.175,
    treadDepth: 0.29
  }]
}
```

## Implementation

- Inherits from `CreateElementsCommandBase` (same pattern as CreateWalls, CreateBeams, etc.)
- Builds the baseline polyline in `memo.stairBaseLine` with proper `API_StairPolylineData` allocation (coords, pends, parcs, edgeData, vertexData)
- Frees default baseline handles before allocating new ones
- Edge/vertex data typed as `APISP_BaseLine` with proper geometry types

## Notes

- This is a minimal but functional first version — additional parameters (walking line position, baseline offset, stair rules, structure types) can be added in follow-up PRs
- No version guards needed — `API_StairType` and `API_StairPolylineData` are stable across AC25-AC29

title: API.GetPropertyValuesOfElements with valid-format parameters crashes ArchiCAD host (no error response)
body:
## Bug Report

**Tapir version:** 1.4.0 (AC29 Mac, build 3100)
**ArchiCAD:** 29 build 4006, USA edition
**OS:** macOS (Apple Silicon / M4)

## Summary

Calling `API.GetPropertyValuesOfElements` with a parameter payload that passes the outer JSON structure check but is incomplete internally causes ArchiCAD to crash rather than returning a clean error response. The HTTP connection is terminated abruptly and the Tapir server goes offline with it.

## Reproduction

```python
import json, urllib.request

data = json.dumps({
    "command": "API.GetPropertyValuesOfElements",
    "parameters": {
        "elements": [{"elementId": {"guid": "VALID-ELEMENT-GUID"}}]
    }
}).encode()

req = urllib.request.Request(
    "http://localhost:19723",
    data=data,
    headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}
)
urllib.request.urlopen(req)  # ArchiCAD crashes, connection closed without response
```

## Expected Behavior

A JSON error response with a schema validation message — consistent with how other commands handle invalid parameters (e.g. `code: 2002`, `"The JSON is invalid according to the JSON schema"`).

## Actual Behavior

ArchiCAD terminates. The Tapir HTTP server goes offline. No error response is returned.

## Context

Other commands with invalid parameters respond correctly with schema errors. This command appears to crash the add-on before the error handler fires, propagating the exception to the host process.

This is a stability concern for automated pipelines that probe available commands or send exploratory requests. A malformed payload to any registered command should not be able to terminate the host application.

Happy to provide the full macOS crash report if useful.

title: CreateFavoritesFromElements creates CornerWindow favorites instead of Window for Hungarian library parts
body:
## Summary

`CreateFavoritesFromElements` creates favorites in the **CornerWindow (Sarokablak)** section of the Favorites palette instead of the **Window (Ablak)** section, for elements placed with the standard Hungarian "ablak" window library part in ArchiCAD 29 HUN.

## Environment

- ArchiCAD 29 Build 4006 HUN (Hungarian localization)
- Teamwork project
- Platform: Windows

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In an ArchiCAD 29 HUN project, place several windows using the standard Hungarian "ablak" library part (placed via the **Window (Ablak)** tool — NOT the Corner Window tool)
2. Call `CreateFavoritesFromElements` via the Tapir API on those window element GUIDs
3. Open the Favorites palette in ArchiCAD

## Expected Behavior

The created favorites should appear under the **Window (Ablak)** section, matching the tool type used to place the elements.

## Actual Behavior

The created favorites appear under the **CornerWindow (Sarokablak)** section instead, even though none of the elements were placed with the Corner Window tool.

Manually creating a favorite for the same element via right-click → "Save as Favorite" correctly places it in the Window section.

## Root Cause

The Hungarian "ablak" library part (and similarly "trapézablak", "kétszárnyú tolóablak") uses `parentUnID = A7D46BBD`, which is a **dual-use GDL part** that supports both regular Window and Corner Window placement.

When `CreateFavoritesFromElements` calls `ACAPI_Element_Get` on such an element, the API returns `header.variationID = APIVarId_CornerWindow ('CRWD')` — even when the element was placed as a regular window (`ac_cw_function == 0`).

Tapir passes this uncorrected `variationID` directly to `ACAPI_Favorite_Create`, causing all favorites to be classified as CornerWindow.

Note: The "Egyszerű ablaknyílás" (Simple Window Opening) library part uses `parentUnID = BCEF86BC` (not a Corner Window subtype) and is **not affected** — favorites created from it correctly appear in the Window section.

## Suggested Fix

Before calling `ACAPI_Favorite_Create`, check `ac_cw_function` and reset the `variationID` if the element is not actually a corner window:

```cpp
// In CreateFavoritesFromElements, before ACAPI_Favorite_Create:
if (element.window.ac_cw_function == 0) {
    element.header.variationID = APIVarId_Generic; // or the appropriate Window variationID
}
```

## Workaround

Manually create each favorite through the ArchiCAD GUI: select element → right-click → Save as Favorite. This correctly classifies the favorite as Window type.

Automated workaround via API is not currently possible, as `DeleteFavorites` also appears to be non-functional (returns `{}` without effect).

## Impact

This bug affects all ArchiCAD 29 HUN projects using standard Hungarian library window parts, making it impossible to programmatically create correctly-typed Window favorites via the Tapir API.

body:
Extend `ChangeWindow` with `navigatorItemId` so you can use Views. 

Extends the existing `ChangeWindow` command with an optional `navigatorItemId` parameter. When given, the navigator item is resolved and (on AC27+) routed through `ACAPI_View_GoToView` so the View's saved settings (layer  scale, zoom) etc. are applied. The existing `databaseId` path is unchanged.

This is an alternative to #394 which provides higher level features on top of the lower level ACAPI calls, we will abandon 394 if we like this approach.


## Schema change

```diff
 {
   "windowType":      { "$ref": "#/WindowType" },
   "databaseId":      { "$ref": "#/DatabaseId" },
+  "navigatorItemId": { "$ref": "#/NavigatorItemId" }
 }
 required: ["windowType"]
```

- Existing callers continue to work unchanged.
- `databaseId` and `navigatorItemId` are mutually exclusive (clear error if both given).
- `windowType` remains required and is validated against the navigator item's database type 

## Behavior

| Input | AC27+ | AC25 / AC26 |
|---|---|---|
| `windowType` only | existing | existing |
| `windowType` + `databaseId` | existing | existing |
| `windowType` + `navigatorItemId` (view) | **`ACAPI_View_GoToView` — view settings applied** | rejected with `NOTSUPPORTED` (use `databaseId` instead) |
| `windowType` + `navigatorItemId` (viewpoint) | `GoToView` (functionally equivalent to a window switch) | rejected with `NOTSUPPORTED` (use `databaseId` instead) |
| `windowType` + `navigatorItemId` (container/folder) | rejected with `BADPARS` | rejected with `NOTSUPPORTED` (version check happens before item-type check) |

## Example

`archicad-addon/Examples/change_window_to_view.py` — enumerates the View Map via `API.GetNavigatorItemTree`, finds the first leaf view, and activates it via `ChangeWindow` with `navigatorItemId`.

title: Fix/element creation crash hardening
body:
# Fix crashes in element-creation commands (slab null-deref, roof hang, polygon/owner guards)

## Summary
While exercising every `Create*` element command against Archicad 29 (Win, build 3000), a few inputs **crashed or hung Archicad** rather than returning an error. This PR fixes them and hardens the create/modify commands against malformed input. All other creation commands (walls, slabs, columns, beams, meshes, zones, morphs, texts, doors, windows, labels, stairs, openings, sections) create correctly after these changes.

## Fixes

### 1. `CreateSlabs` — null-pointer crash on a valid polygon
`BuildSlabMemoFromGeometry` only (re)allocated the polygon memo handles **when the requested vertex count differed from the active default slab**. But `ACAPI_Element_GetDefaults` can leave `memo.coords == nullptr`, and `BMReallocHandle` does **not** allocate from a null handle (it returns null, unlike C `realloc`). When the requested polygon happened to have the same vertex count as the default slab (e.g. a 4-corner slab on a template whose default slab is also 4 corners), the allocation branch was skipped, `memo.coords` stayed null, and `AddPolyToMemo` dereferenced it → access violation.

**Fix:** allocate fresh with `BMAllocateHandle`/`BMAllocatePtr` when the handle is null; only resize an existing handle with `BMReallocHandle`. (Data-dependent, which is why it was easy to miss — a 3- or 5-point slab allocates and works.) The same null-safe allocation is applied to the roof pivot-polygon memo.

### 2. `CreateMeshes` / `CreateZones` — crash on a short/empty polygon
Both called `polygonCoordinates.GetFirst()/GetLast()` **before** any size check, so an empty or `<3`-point polygon crashed. Added the same `< 3` guard `BuildSlabMemoFromGeometry` already uses (returns `APIERR_BADPARS`).

### 3. `CreateRoofs` — throws + modal dialog hangs the JSON API
A multi-plane (`API_PolyRoofID`) roof needs per-edge pivot plane data (`memo.pivotPolyEdges` holding `API_RoofSegmentData`, keyed by the pivot polygon's edge unique IDs) plus a contour polygon. These are not built, so `ACAPI_Element_Create` rejects the element by **throwing a `GSException` and popping a modal `Information` dialog** that blocks the JSON API until dismissed. As shipped, any `CreateRoofs` call hangs/crashes the host.

**Fix (interim):** reject `CreateRoofs` with a clear structured error instead of calling `Create`, so it can never crash or hang. Completing real multi-plane roof creation (building `pivotPolyEdges`) is left as follow-up — happy to do it in a separate PR if there's interest.

### 4. Required-field hardening (defense-in-depth)
Several commands dereference `*data.Get("requiredField")` / `*item.Get("elementId")` directly. Archicad's dispatcher schema-validates parameters before the add-on runs, so these are normally unreachable, but a schema/code mismatch or a non-validating caller would crash. Guarded the required-field dereferences across walls, beams, doors, windows, openings, morphs, the dimension commands, sections, and the `Modify*` commands (return a structured error / push a failed-item result instead of dereferencing null).

## Testing
Built `RelWithDebInfo` (AC29, VS2022 v143) with zero warnings under the project's `/W4 /WX`. Verified live on Archicad 29: all listed creation commands create correctly; the slab/mesh/zone cases that previously crashed now succeed; `CreateRoofs` returns a clean error; and a malformed-input pass (missing required fields) returns errors with Archicad staying responsive throughout.

## Notes
- The fixes are split into two commits (polygon guards; extended-creation hardening) and can be split into separate PRs if preferred.
- Root cause of the slab crash was confirmed from a crash dump (access violation, read from `0x0`, faulting frame `AddPolyToMemo` writing `*memo.coords`).

title: Feature request: Add LockElements and UnlockElements commands
body:
## Problem

Tapir currently supports layer locking through `CreateLayers`, but it does not expose Archicad's element-level lock and unlock operations.

Unlocking a layer is not sufficient when elements are individually locked. In our tested case, the layer was successfully changed to `isLocked: false`, but the elements still failed the `IsEditable` filter and could not be deleted through `DeleteElements`.

## Use case

Automation workflows may need to modify or delete individually locked elements. A typical sequence is:

1. Query elements with `GetAllElements` or `GetElementsByType`.
2. Unlock their layer if necessary.
3. Unlock the individual elements.
4. Modify or delete them.

Without step 3, the workflow cannot be completed through Tapir.

## Archicad C++ API

The public Archicad Add-On API provides this capability through:

```cpp
ACAPI_Grouping_Tool (elementGuids, APITool_Unlock, nullptr);
ACAPI_Grouping_Tool (elementGuids, APITool_Lock, nullptr);
```

Reference: https://graphisoft.github.io/archicad-api-devkit/group___grouping.html

## Proposed commands

- `LockElements`
- `UnlockElements`

Suggested input:

```json
{
  "elements": [
    {
      "elementId": {
        "guid": "A2FCFB91-CBBB-4835-A052-B41471C7B7E5"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Suggested behavior:

- Execute inside an undoable command scope.
- Return execution results or errors, preferably per element where practical.
- Support Archicad 27 and later if the API signatures permit it.
- Keep group handling explicit; optionally document whether group suspension is required.

I am interested in implementing this and submitting a pull request. Would this command naming and schema fit Tapir's architecture?

## Environment

- Archicad 27 GER, build 6000
- Tapir 1.5.0
- Windows
- Door favorites are present and returned by `GetFavoritesByType`
- Standard/project libraries are loaded

## Problem

Both `CreateDoors` and `CreateWindows` fail with error code `-2130313110` (`APIERR_REFUSEDPAR`) on a valid, editable host wall.

The Door case still fails when a valid Door favorite is supplied. Applying the same favorite through `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults` reports success, but a subsequent `CreateDoors` call without `favoriteName` also fails.

## Minimal reproduction

Create a straight editable wall, then call:

```json
{
  "doorsData": [
    {
      "ownerWallId": {
        "guid": "<valid-wall-guid>"
      },
      "centerOffset": 1.25,
      "sillHeight": 0.0,
      "width": 1.01,
      "height": 2.26,
      "favoriteName": "hma 1-Fl. Holz/ Stahlblechtür"
    }
  ]
}
```

Result:

```text
CreateDoors failed: Failed to create door. (code -2130313110)
```

The same host wall successfully accepts a generic `CreateOpenings` element, so the wall, position, dimensions, editability and project state are valid.

## Additional observations

- `GetFavoritesByType(Door)` returns seven valid Door favorites.
- `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults` for the selected Door favorite returns `{ "success": true }`.
- `GetFavoritesByType(Window)` returns no Window favorites in this project, but Door creation fails even though a Door favorite exists.
- Tapir 1.5.1 appears to contain the same Door/Window creation code as 1.5.0.

## Suspected area

`PrepareWindowOrDoorDefaults` first calls `ACAPI_Element_GetDefaultsExt`, which should return the favorite-applied element, memo and marker. It then retrieves the generic marker parent and replaces `marker.memo.params` with parameters from that library part.

Could this second marker construction produce a marker/libpart mismatch on Archicad 27? A useful experiment may be to preserve the marker returned by `GetDefaultsExt` when it is valid, rather than replacing its parameters.

## Suggested improvements

- Preserve and validate the marker returned by `ACAPI_Element_GetDefaultsExt`.
- Return more diagnostics on failure: selected opening libpart index/name, marker libpart index/name, owner wall type/editability and whether defaults/favorite application succeeded.
- Add an Archicad 27 regression test for favorite-based Door/Window creation.

title: Feature request: expose Zone Stamp rotation angle in CreateZones / SetDetailsOfElements
body:
### Summary
Please add an optional **zone stamp rotation angle** parameter to `CreateZones` (and ideally to `SetDetailsOfElements` for zones, so it can be changed after creation).

### Context
I'm building a pipeline that reads a DXF floor-plan sketch and models it in Archicad through Tapir (walls, slabs, zones). Each room name is a `TEXT`/`MTEXT` entity in the DXF and **carries its own rotation** — e.g. narrow rooms like a corridor have the label drawn at 90°. I can read that angle from the DXF, but I cannot reproduce it on the created zone, because the **zone stamp keeps the default (horizontal) orientation**.

In the Archicad UI this is the setting **"Zone Stamp Rotation Angle"** (Zone Selection Settings → *Zone Stamp* → *Zone Stamp Rotation Angle*, with a Relative/Absolute toggle). It also appears in the Info Box when a zone is selected.

### Current state (verified on Tapir 1.5.0 / Archicad 26)
The stamp angle does not seem to be reachable from the JSON/Python API:

- `CreateZones` → `zonesData` has `name`, `numberStr`, `categoryAttributeId`, `stampPosition`, `geometry`, `floorIndex` — **no angle**.
- `SetDetailsOfElements` → zone `typeSpecificDetails` returns/accepts name, numberStr, categoryAttributeId, stampPosition, polygonOutline, holes — **no angle**.
- `GetGDLParametersOfElements` on a zone → the stamp angle is **not** among the GDL parameters.
- Official API built-in properties → there is `IdAndCategories_ZoneStampName` but **no** zone-stamp angle/rotation property.

### Request
Add an optional field to `zonesData`, e.g.:

```json
"stampRotationAngle": 90.0,        // degrees
"stampRotationIsRelative": true    // optional; mirrors the UI Relative/Absolute toggle
```

and expose the same in `SetDetailsOfElements` zone `typeSpecificDetails` so existing zones can be updated.

In the C++ Add-On API this corresponds to the zone stamp angle field of `API_ZoneType`.

### Why it matters
Without it, every rotated room label has to be fixed by hand after an otherwise fully-automated import. Exposing the angle would make DXF/CAD → Archicad zone import lossless.

### Summary
On **Tapir 1.5.2**, calling **`CreateDoors` / `CreateWindows` with more than one item in a single call crashes Archicad** (the application closes unexpectedly). The Python client then fails on the *next* command with `ConnectionResetError [WinError 10054]`, because Archicad has already died.

Creating the **exact same openings one at a time** (one item per `CreateDoors`/`CreateWindows` call) works perfectly — no crash.

This is a **regression**: the same batched calls worked on **Tapir 1.5.0**.

### Environment
- Tapir **1.5.2** (AC26 Win, `TapirAddOn_AC26_Win.apx`)
- Archicad **26** (INT/PTB), Windows 11
- Python `archicad` package, JSON/Python API

### Steps to reproduce
1. Create a few host walls (`CreateWalls`, batched — this is fine).
2. Call `CreateDoors` with a `doorsData` array containing **several** doors (each with `ownerWallId`, `centerOffset`, `width`, `height`, `sillHeight`, `favoriteName`, and the new `reflected`/`oSide`). 
3. The command returns, but **Archicad crashes a moment later** (apparently during regeneration). The next API call fails with `ConnectionResetError [WinError 10054]`.

Create the openings **one per call**:
```python
for d in doorsData:
    ExecuteAddOnCommand(CreateDoors, {"doorsData": [d]})   # one item -> OK
```
A diagnostic that created 7 doors + 5 windows one-by-one (with a `GetAddOnVersion` health-check after each) completed with Archicad staying alive the whole time. The identical set sent as two batched calls reliably crashes Archicad.

### Notes
- The items use `favoriteName` plus the new `reflected`/`oSide` fields from #409. I did not isolate whether the crash needs those fields or just the multi-item array, but on 1.5.0 multi-item batches (with `favoriteName`) did not crash — so something between 1.5.0 and 1.5.2 introduced it. - Native JSON server → `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand` → `TapirCommand.SetStories`

## Steps to reproduce

Open a project with a basement, e.g. `UG (index -1, level -3.0)`, `EG (index 0, level 0.0)`, `OG (index 1, level 3.0)`. `GetStories` reports `firstStory: -1`.

Send `SetStories` with the same three stories but `OG.level = 3.25`:

```json
{ "stories": [
  {"index": -1, "dispOnSections": true,  "level": -3.0, "name": "UG"},
  {"index": 0,  "dispOnSections": false, "level": 0.0,  "name": "EG"},
  {"index": 1,  "dispOnSections": true,  "level": 3.25, "name": "OG"}
]}
```

Result:

```json
{"success": false, "error": {"code": -2130313112, "message": "Failed to change story level."}}
```

OG stays at 3.0. Deleting a story (sending fewer stories than exist) fails the same way with `"Failed to delete story."`.

A project whose stories all start at index 0 (no basement) does **not** reproduce — there the array position coincidentally equals the real story index.

## Evidence that the wrong story is targeted

On the basement project (after also inserting a 4th story so a level change isn't the top story), requesting a level change on the **EG** entry only (array position 1) leaves EG unchanged and instead moves **OG** (real index 1) to the requested value. So the command operates on the story at the array position, not the intended story — exactly the off‑by‑`-firstStory` shift.

## Root cause

In `archicad-addon/Sources/ProjectCommands.cpp`, `SetStoriesCommand::Execute`, the modify loop (~L574) and delete loop (~L549) do:

```cpp
const API_StoryType& story = (*storyInfo.data)[i];
...
storyCmd.index = static_cast<short>(i);   // array position 0..n-1
```

`storyInfo.data[]` is ordered `firstStory..lastStory`, so the real index is `(*storyInfo.data)[i].index` (= `i + firstStory`). When `firstStory == 0` the two coincide; when `firstStory < 0` (a basement) the index is off by `-firstStory`, and `ACAPI_ProjectSetting_ChangeStorySettings` is applied to the wrong or a non‑existent story.

The insert branch is unaffected because it uses `storyInfo.lastStory` (a real index).

## Suggested fix

Use the real story index in both loops, e.g.:

```cpp
storyCmd.index = (*storyInfo.data)[i].index;   // instead of static_cast<short>(i)
```

This has been present since 1.5.0. Happy to open a PR if that helps.

title: fix(stories): SetStories uses array position instead of real story index (breaks with basements)

`SetStoriesCommand::Execute` passed the **array position** in `storyInfo.data[]` as `API_StoryCmdType.index`, but that field must be the **actual** (possibly negative) story index. | insert a 4th story | wrong/failed | success, created at requested level |
| delete back to 3 stories | `Failed to delete story` | success |

title: CreateStairs: stepNum / treadDepth / riserHeight are ignored — run length is fixed regardless of parameters
body:
## Summary

`CreateStairs` accepts `stepNum`, `treadDepth` and `riserHeight` in its schema and writes them to the element, but the created stair's geometry does not reflect them: the **run length is fixed regardless of the values sent** (and independent of the `baseLinePoints` segment length). This makes it impossible to fit a straight native stair into a run shorter than the auto-computed length (e.g. a 3.27 m room — the stair overshoots).

## Environment

- Tapir 1.5.x (build off current `main`), Archicad 28, Windows
- Native JSON server → `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand` → `TapirCommand.CreateStairs`

## Steps to reproduce

Create straight stairs on the same baseline with different parameters, then measure the plan footprint via `Get3DBoundingBoxes` (the stair's y-extent along the baseline = run length):

| stepNum | treadDepth | totalHeight | run length (footprint y-extent) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 13 | 0.30 | 3.25 | 4.65 m |
| 20 | 0.20 | 3.25 | 4.65 m |
| (none) | 0.30 | 3.25 | 4.65 m |
| (none) | 0.20 | 3.25 | 4.65 m |
| (none) | 0.15 | 3.25 | 4.65 m |

The run length stays ~4.65 m in every case.

## What I tried

`CreateStairsCommand::SetTypeSpecificParameters` does set the fields (`element.stair.stepNum / treadDepth / riserHeight = …`). I also prototyped setting the lock flags `element.stair.treadDepthLocked = true` and `element.stair.totalHeightLocked = true` whenever the corresponding parameter is provided — the run length **still** did not change (0.15 / 0.20 / 0.30 all produced 4.65 m).

## Question

It looks like the stair geometry is regenerated from the baseline + the rule (`API_StairRulesData` — e.g. `treadDepthMinValue`/`treadDepthMaxValue` and the 2R+G rule) during `ACAPI_Element_Create`, so the scalar `treadDepth`/`stepNum` aren't honored as inputs. Is there a supported way to force a specific going / step count / run length via the API (configuring `rules`, a rule type, the `tread[]` data, …), or is this a current API limitation? If you can point me at the right mechanism I'm happy to implement it.

Minor, related: `Get3DBoundingBoxes` returns only the footprint for stairs (`zMax = 0`), so the 3D height can't be read back / verified via the API.

title: CreateWalls crashes Archicad on a zero-length wall (begCoordinate == endCoordinate)
body:
## Summary

`CreateWalls` with a wall whose `begCoordinate` equals `endCoordinate` (zero-length / degenerate wall) **crashes Archicad** instead of rejecting the input. Observed reproducibly on **Archicad 26 (Win)** during a batched `CreateWalls` call: after a number of valid walls, the first zero-length entry takes Archicad down (process exits, the Python client then fails with a connection reset on the next command).

This is nasty because a single bad coordinate pair in an otherwise-valid batch aborts the whole session and can lose work.

## Environment

- Tapir 1.5.3 (AC26 Win); also relevant for other versions
- Native JSON server → `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand` → `TapirCommand.CreateWalls`

## How it happens

Source plans whose corner axes collapse during processing can produce wall segments where `beg == end`. Such entries pass schema validation (both coordinates are present and well-formed) and are handed straight to `ACAPI_Element_Create`, which crashes on the degenerate geometry rather than returning an error.

A batch with even one such wall crashes; the same batch with the zero-length entries removed completes fine.

## Root cause

`CreateWallsCommand::SetTypeSpecificParameters` (`archicad-addon/Sources/ExtendedElementCommands.cpp`) reads `begCoordinate`/`endCoordinate` and assigns them to `element.wall.begC`/`endC` without checking that they differ. There is no degeneracy guard before `ACAPI_Element_Create`.

## Suggested fix

Reject zero-length walls in the handler so the bad item returns an error (and is skipped) instead of crashing — using the existing `IsSame2DCoordinate` helper:

```cpp
API_Coord begCoordinate = Get2DCoordinateFromObjectState (*parameters.Get ("begCoordinate"));
API_Coord endCoordinate = Get2DCoordinateFromObjectState (*parameters.Get ("endCoordinate"));

if (IsSame2DCoordinate (begCoordinate, endCoordinate)) {
    return CreateErrorResponse (APIERR_BADPARS, "Zero-length wall: 'begCoordinate' and 'endCoordinate' are identical.");
}
```

Because `CreateWalls` is array-in / array-out, the offending wall then yields an `ErrorItem` in its slot and the rest of the batch still succeeds — no crash. I have this change ready and can open a PR if you'd like. (`ModifyWalls` may deserve the same guard for `begCoordinate`/`endCoordinate` edits.)

title: Add drawIndex repositioning to SetDetailsOfElements
body:
_Since this is a workaround for an Archicad limitation, it may not meet the quality standards we want for Tapir, in which case we may choose not to include it.
I’ve also discovered some pretty surprising limitations related to Archicad (not even a C++ API issue) in this regard. I now understand better why there isn’t a direct command to change the display order. The modified command attempts to work around these limitations._

## What this does

Adds `drawIndex` support to `SetDetailsOfElements`. Setting `drawIndex`
via `ACAPI_Element_Change` is silently ignored by ArchiCAD (confirmed
Graphisoft bug in AC27), so repositioning is implemented via
`ACAPI_Grouping_Tool`.

## Implementation

**Normal elements** — two strategies, cheapest (fewest API calls) wins:
- *Direct*: step-by-step `BringForward` / `SendBackward`
- *ViaReset*: `ResetOrder` to class default, then step to target

**Door / Window / Skylight** — special host manipulation:
ArchiCAD enforces a hard minimum of level 7 for openings embedded in a
host (Door/Window in Wall, Skylight in Roof or Shell). Levels 8–14 are
reached by stepping the host element up (the opening follows), then
stepping it back down (the opening stays elevated). Reset (`drawIndex=0`)
on an elevated opening must also go through the host. The host is found
via a forward scan of all walls/roofs/shells with
`GetConnectedElements`. Within each batch, openings are processed before
all other elements so the host manipulation always starts from the
host's natural position.

**Dead ends (do not reintroduce):**
- `APITool_BringToFront` — unreliable on Wall and its sub-elements
- `APITool_SendToBack` — does not reliably reach level 1 in sparse files

## Known limitations

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Door/Window/Skylight, levels 1–6 | Unreachable (ArchiCAD constraint, min = 7) |
| Opening below its host's current level | Unreachable |
| Multiple openings in the same host, different targets, same batch | All end up at the same level (last processed wins) |
| `Opening` (API_OpeningID, generic void) | Fully immovable — all Grouping_Tool calls are no-ops; ArchiCAD displays level 0 for these elements |
| Morph / Railing / PolyLine, `drawIndex=0` | `ResetOrder` is a no-op; simulated via step-by-step to class default |

title: BUG: CreateSlabs crashes ArchiCAD on multi-slab requests (vertex-count dependent)
body:
## Summary

A `CreateSlabs` request that contains more than one slab reliably crashes
ArchiCAD. The process terminates and the JSON connection closes mid-request
(`Remote end closed connection without response`); ArchiCAD must be restarted.
A request with a single slab never crashes, regardless of the slab's
complexity.

Isolating the variables shows the crash is tied to the slabs' outer vertex
count, not to the number of slabs, geometry validity, holes, or curves:

1. A multi-slab request is reliable only when every slab has the same vertex
   count and that count is low (at or below 11 in this data set).
2. Mixing different vertex counts in one request crashes, even when all the
   counts are small.
3. A homogeneous request of high-vertex-count slabs (12 or more here) crashes
   with as few as 2 slabs, even though a homogeneous request of 185 four-vertex
   slabs succeeds.

This suggests a per-request buffer or allocation problem in the multi-element
handling of `CreateSlabs`, for example a memo sized from one slab and then
reused across slabs that have a different or larger vertex count.

## Environment

- ArchiCAD build: 28.4.0 (7006) AUS FULL
- OS: macOS 15.7.7 (Apple Silicon)
- Tapir version 1.5.3
- Tapir `CreateSlabs` command version 1.0.3
- Requests sent to the JSON API on localhost, wrapped in
  `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand` with `commandNamespace: "TapirCommand"`,
  `commandName: "CreateSlabs"`.

## Request and response shape

Single-slab request (always succeeds):

```json
{
  "command": "API.ExecuteAddOnCommand",
  "parameters": {
    "addOnCommandId": { "commandNamespace": "TapirCommand", "commandName": "CreateSlabs" },
    "addOnCommandParameters": {
      "slabsData": [
        {
          "level": 168.98,
          "thickness": 7.0,
          "referencePlaneLocation": "Bottom",
          "polygonCoordinates": [
            {"x": -478.37, "y": -23.95},
            {"x": -471.52, "y": -25.58},
            {"x": -471.07, "y": -23.68},
            {"x": -477.92, "y": -22.05}
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Success response:

```json
{"succeeded": true, "result": {"addOnCommandResponse": {"elements": [{"elementId": {"guid": "..."}}]}}}
```

On a crash no JSON is returned: the HTTP connection closes and the client
reports `Remote end closed connection without response`.

## Data set for the "real data" scenarios

592 slabs, all `referencePlaneLocation: "Bottom"`, positive thickness, valid
closed rings. Outer vertex-count distribution:

```
3v x2, 4v x185, 5v x5, 6v x63, 7v x13, 8v x74, 9v x13, 10v x48, 11v x17,
12v x49, 13v x21, 14v x26, 15v x9, 16v x23, 17v x8, 18v x10, 19v x5, 20v x6,
21v x3, 22v x1, 23v x4, 25v x1, 26v x2, 28v x2, 29v x1, 53v x1
```

## Scenarios

### Scenario 1: synthetic, uniform simple slabs, one multi-slab request. Result: OK
10 identical 4-vertex square slabs in a single request, and separately 100
identical 4-vertex squares. `succeeded: true` with all GUIDs returned, no
crash, repeated several times. Many slabs per request are fine when each is
simple and identical.

### Scenario 2: synthetic, varied vertex counts, multi-slab request. Result: CRASH
592 slabs sent in batches of 100; each slab a generated convex polygon with a
random vertex count from 3 to 20 (no holes, valid, CCW). The payload shape is
identical to Scenario 1 except that vertex count varies per slab. Crashes
within the first batch.

### Scenario 3: real data, one slab per request. Result: OK
The 592 real slabs, each sent in its own request (one entry in `slabsData`),
vertex counts 3 to 53, some with holes. All 592 succeeded with zero crashes,
including a 53-vertex slab. Any individual slab is fine regardless of vertex
count or holes.

### Scenario 4: real data, mixed vertex counts in a request. Result: CRASH
The 592 real slabs with several slabs per request and mixed vertex counts:
- all 420 slabs of 11 vertices or fewer in one request (mixed 3 to 11);
- batches of 100, 10, and 2 (mixed counts).
Every case crashes on the first multi-slab request, including the batch of 2.
Mixing different vertex counts crashes even when every slab is small.

### Scenario 5: real data, grouped by exact vertex count (homogeneous). Result: OK at or below 11v, CRASH at 12v
The 592 slabs bucketed by exact outer vertex count, each bucket sent as one
request so every request is vertex-count-homogeneous:
- groups of 3 to 11 vertices all succeeded, including large single requests of
  185 x 4v, 74 x 8v, 63 x 6v, 48 x 10v, and 17 x 11v;
- the 12-vertex group (49 slabs) in one request crashed.

### Scenario 6: real data, homogeneous high-vertex group, shrinking request size. Result: CRASH until size 1
The 12-vertex group (49 slabs, all exactly 12 vertices):
- 20 per request: crash (first 20);
- 2 per request: crash (first 2);
- 1 per request: OK. Every group from 12v up to 53v, sent one slab per request,
  succeeded.

## Key observations

- Single-slab requests never crashed (any vertex count or holes; 53v confirmed).
- Homogeneous multi-slab requests succeed for slabs of 11 vertices or fewer even
  at 185 slabs per request, but a homogeneous request of 12-vertex slabs crashes
  at just 2 slabs. The discriminator is vertex count, not slab count.
- Mixed-vertex-count multi-slab requests crash even when all counts are small.
- Holes and curves are not required: Scenario 2 used simple, hole-free, valid
  convex polygons and still crashed.

## Suggested minimal repro

1. One request with N identical low-vertex (for example 4-vertex) squares:
   expect success.
2. One request with N identical high-vertex (for example 12-vertex or more)
   polygons, N of 2 or more: expect a crash.
3. One request with a few slabs of differing vertex counts (for example one 4v
   and one 5v): expect a crash.

The 11-versus-12 boundary is specific to this data set. The exact per-request
vertex threshold is worth confirming with a controlled sweep of vertex count
and slab count.

title: Regression: batched CreateSlabs crashes Archicad (per-item works) — same class as #417
body:
### Summary

Batching more than one slab into a single `CreateSlabs` call force-closes ArchiCAD. Creating the same slabs **one per call** succeeds. This looks like the same class of batch-create crash as #417 (`CreateDoors`/`CreateWindows`).

### Environment

- ArchiCAD **28** (German), Windows
- Tapir **1.5.3**
- Python `archicad` package (JSON/Python API)

### Symptom

A batched `CreateSlabs` (10 slabs in one call) terminates ArchiCAD outright — the process exits and the next command from the Python client fails with `ConnectionResetError: [WinError 10054]`. No graceful per-item error is returned; the whole session (and unsaved work) is lost.

### Steps / context

Our converter builds a storey model, then walls, then slabs. The crash reproduces like this:

1. `CreateWalls` for ~68 walls, each with a **non-center `referenceLineLocation`** (`CoreOutside`/`CoreInside`, the field added in 1.5.3). All succeed.
2. `CreateSlabs` with **10 slabs in one call** → ArchiCAD crashes.

Isolating the slab phase (same project state, same 68 reference-line walls already placed):

- `CreateSlabs` called **one slab per call** → all 10 created successfully, no crash.
- `CreateSlabs` called **batched (10 in one call)** → crash.

Interestingly, in an earlier run where the walls were created with the **default (centered) reference line**, the identical batched `CreateSlabs(10)` call worked. So the crash appears to be **project-state dependent** — it reproduces once the project contains walls with a non-center reference line — which mirrors the state/locale dependence reported in #417.

The 10 slabs are plain floors/ceilings (3–12 point polygons, positive thickness, `Basic` structure) — the same data that creates fine one-at-a-time, so the individual slabs are not degenerate.

### Suspected cause

Same area as #417 (batched `CreateDoors`/`CreateWindows` crash, suspected PR #409 / #410 element-creation hardening). Possibly `CreateSlabs` shares the batch-create path that regressed.

### Workaround

Create slabs one per `CreateSlabs` call.

### Notes

I can put together a minimal standalone repro (a tiny script: place a couple of reference-line walls, then a batched `CreateSlabs`) if that would help pin it down — just let me know.

title: Add navigator view/layout commands (CreateLayout, SetLayoutSettings, view map operations)
body:
## Summary

Adds a full set of navigator commands for managing layouts, subsets, and view map items.

### New commands

**Layout Book**
- `CreateLayoutSubset` — create a subset with all numbering options (style, prefix, startAt, continueNumbering…)
- `CreateLayout` — create a layout with full `layoutParameters` (size, margins, numbering, master by name or ID)
- `GetLayoutSettings` — read all layout parameters (works on regular layouts and master layouts)
- `SetLayoutSettings` — modify layout parameters with enforced rules:
  - `horizontalSize` / `verticalSize` only allowed on master layouts
  - `showMasterBelow` verified by read-back (ArchiCAD ignores it silently on regular layouts)

**View Map**
- `CreateViewMapFolder` — create a folder in the View Map
- `CreateViewsInViewMap` — create independent views from Project Map items
- `CreateViewMapCloneFolder` — create a live-sync clone folder mirroring a Project Map folder
- `SetViewRotation` — set rotation (radians) on one or more views
- `GetViewSettings` — read view parameters (rotation, structureDisplay, saveZoom, d3styleName…)
- `SetViewSettings` — modify view parameters
- `GetView2DTransformations` — read DB-level zoom/rotation (independent of per-view rotation)

**Navigator (shared)**
- `RenameNavigatorItem` — rename any navigator item
- `MoveNavigatorItem` — move with optional `previousNavigatorItemId` for ordering
- `DeleteNavigatorItems` — delete layouts, views, folders (subsets not supported by AC API)

### AC25/AC26 compatibility

All new functions (`ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeNavigatorItem`, `SetNavigatorItemPosition`, `DeleteNavigatorView`, `SearchNavigatorItem`, `ACAPI_Database_DeleteDatabase`, `ACAPI_Element_GetExtent`) were introduced in AC27. ### Design notes

- `IsMasterLayoutDatabase()` helper detects master vs regular layout via `ACAPI_Navigator_SearchNavigatorItem` (checking `result.itemType == API_MasterLayoutNavItem`), because `DatabaseIdResolver::GetDatabaseWithId()` always returns `typeID = 0`.
- `showMasterBelow` is verified by read-back after `ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeLayoutSets` since AC silently ignores it on regular layouts.

| `test_layout_workflow.py` | CreateLayoutSubset (all options), CreateLayout (all params), GetLayoutSettings, SetLayoutSettings (all restrictions), RenameNavigatorItem, MoveNavigatorItem, DeleteNavigatorItems |

title: Feature request: Read and modify placement (position, scale, source link) of Drawing elements
body:
## Summary
There is currently no way to programmatically read the geometry (position, size, scale) 
or the source link of a Drawing element that has already been placed on a Layout. 
There is also no way to change/relink the source of an existing Drawing.

## What already works
- `CreateDrawings` can create a new Drawing linked to a navigator item, at a given 
  position and scale.
- `UpdateDrawings` can refresh the content of an existing Drawing from its current source.

## What is missing
- `GetDetailsOfElements` returns `{"error": "Not yet supported element type"}` when 
  called on a Drawing element.
- `Get2DBoundingBoxes` / `Get3DBoundingBoxes` return `{"error": "Element not supported"}` 
  for Drawing elements.
- There is no command to change the source (navigator item / view) that an existing 
  Drawing is linked to (the equivalent of the native "Link Drawing to..." command).

## Use case
We want to automate a repetitive workflow: on a template layout, a set of Drawings 
(floor plan excerpts) is manually arranged at specific positions/scales, each linked 
to a specific view. We then need to replicate that exact arrangement across many other 
layouts, but each time linking the Drawings to a different (but equivalently structured) 
set of views. Since the arrangement varies per project and can't be hardcoded, we need to:
1. Read the position, size, and scale of each Drawing on the template layout.
2. Either update the link of an existing Drawing, or recreate it with `CreateDrawings` 
   using the same geometry but a different source.

Since the underlying C++ API (`API_DrawingType`) already exposes anchor point, width, 
height and linked source, it seems like the geometry data is available internally – 
it's just not yet exposed through the JSON/Python commands.

## Requested commands (naming is just a suggestion)
- `GetDrawingParameters(elements)` → returns position, size, scale, and current 
  linked source (navigator item) for each given Drawing element.
- `ChangeDrawingLink(elements_with_new_source)` → relinks an existing Drawing to a 
  different navigator item, keeping its position/size/scale unchanged.

Happy to help test this if it gets implemented. Thanks for maintaining this great add-on!

title: fix(walls): reject zero-length walls in CreateWalls instead of crashing
body:
## Summary

Fixes #433. `CreateWalls` with a wall whose `begCoordinate == endCoordinate` (zero length) **crashes Archicad** (access violation, connection reset) instead of returning an error. This happens easily with real source data when axis/corner intersection collapses a segment.

## Change

Guard at the top of `CreateWallsCommand::SetTypeSpecificParameters`: if begin and end coordinates are the same (via the existing `IsSame2DCoordinate` helper), return a controlled `APIERR_BADPARS` error for that item instead of proceeding into `ACAPI_Element_Create` (which crashes). Other walls in the same batch are unaffected — they still succeed, and the offending item gets an error entry in the result, consistent with the command's existing per-item error handling.

```cpp
if (IsSame2DCoordinate (begCoordinate, endCoordinate)) {
    return CreateErrorResponse (APIERR_BADPARS, "Zero-length wall: 'begCoordinate' and 'endCoordinate' are identical.");
}
```

## Testing

- Built clean on AC26 and AC28 (Win, VS2019, DevKit 26.3000 / 28.3001).
- Before: a batch containing a zero-length wall force-closed Archicad (reproduced on AC26, ~18 walls in, matching #433).
- After: the zero-length item returns `APIERR_BADPARS` with the message above; the remaining walls in the batch are created normally; no crash.

Mirrors the existing degenerate-polygon guards elsewhere in this file (slabs/zones use `IsSame2DCoordinate` the same way).

title: CreateStairs: multi-segment baselines (L/U-shaped) always fail with error -2130313215
body:
## Summary
`CreateStairs` (added in 1.5.0, PR #388) works for straight (2-point) baselines but **fails for every multi-segment baseline** (L-shaped and U-shaped) with:

```json
{"elements":[{"error":{"code":-2130313215,"message":"Failed to create new Stair"}}]}
```

PR #388 states the implementation covers "straight and multi-segment stairs (L-shaped, U-shaped)".

## Environment
- Tapir 1.5.3
- Archicad 28 build 7006 INT (Intel-based Mac build, running on Apple Silicon via Rosetta)
- macOS 15.x (Darwin 25.5.0)

## Steps to reproduce
Straight baseline — **works**:
```json
{"stairsData":[{"baseLinePoints":[{"x":10.0,"y":0.0},{"x":16.3,"y":0.0}],"zCoordinate":0.0,"totalHeight":3.40,"flightWidth":1.20}]}
```

L-shaped — **fails**:
```json
{"stairsData":[{"baseLinePoints":[{"x":20.0,"y":0.0},{"x":20.0,"y":4.0},{"x":24.0,"y":4.0}],"zCoordinate":0.0,"totalHeight":3.40,"flightWidth":1.20}]}
```

U-shaped — **fails**:
```json
{"stairsData":[{"baseLinePoints":[{"x":0.6,"y":0.0},{"x":0.6,"y":3.9},{"x":2.0,"y":3.9},{"x":2.0,"y":0.0}],"zCoordinate":0.0,"totalHeight":3.40,"flightWidth":1.20}]}
```

## Variants tried (all fail identically)
- With and without the optional parameters (`totalHeight`, `flightWidth`, `stepNum`, `riserHeight`, `treadDepth`)
- Consistent riser/tread/height combinations (22 x 0.16818 = 3.70)
- Larger geometry (legs 4-5 m, cross segments 1.4 / 2.0 / 2.5 m)
- Only the required parameters (`baseLinePoints` + `zCoordinate`)

Straight baselines succeed every time with the same tool defaults, so the default Stair settings solve fine.

Possibly related: #403, #425.

title: fix(stairs): support multi-segment (L/U-shaped) baselines in CreateStairs
body:
## Summary

Fixes #444. `CreateStairs` (from #388) failed with `-2130313215 "Failed to create new Stair"` for **every** multi-segment (L-shaped / U-shaped) baseline, while straight 2-point baselines worked.

## Root cause

`SetTypeSpecificParameters` pre-filled `stairBaseLine.edgeData` / `vertexData` by hand. The allocation is cleared, so `segmentType` stayed `0` = `APIST_StepsSegment` on **every** edge. A multi-segment baseline whose corner edges are forced to be steps segments is unsolvable for the stair solver, so `ACAPI_Element_Create` rejected all L/U baselines.

## Change

Leave `edgeData`/`vertexData` null and let `ACAPI_Element_Create` derive them from the baseline geometry — the same pattern as the `Element_Test` example in the API DevKit (`Do_CreateStair` sets only `coords`/`parcs`/`polygon`). Net −10 lines.

## Testing (live against AC28, Win)

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Straight 2-point baseline (regression) | ✅ | ✅ unchanged (footprint 1.2 × 4.65 at totalHeight 3.4) |
| L-shaped 3-point baseline (issue repro) | ❌ `-2130313215` | ✅ stair created |
| U-shaped 4-point baseline, legs 3.0 m apart | ❌ `-2130313215` | ✅ stair created |
| U-shaped, legs only 1.4 m apart (issue's exact coordinates) | ❌ | ❌ solver error — expected: the flights/landings physically don't fit between legs that close (the UI rejects this geometry too) |

So after the fix the remaining `-2130313215` cases are genuine "stair rules cannot solve this geometry" results (per-item error, other items in the batch unaffected), not a blanket multi-segment failure.

Built clean on AC26 and AC28 (Win, VS2019, DevKit 26.3000 / 28.3001).

title: fix(walls,columns): explicit height overrides story top-link
body:
## Summary

`CreateColumns` with `height: 2.0` produces a 2.65 m column when the template's column tool default is top-linked to a story — the explicit value is silently ignored. The same template dependence is behind long-standing "`CreateWalls` `height` is not honored" reports: whether an explicit height works currently depends on whether the tool default happens to be story-linked.

## Root cause

`CreateWalls`, `CreateColumns`, `ModifyWalls` and `ModifyColumns` write `element.wall.height` / `element.column.height` but never touch **`relativeTopStory`**. When the default is top-linked (`relativeTopStory > 0`), Archicad derives the element height from the link and ignores the field.

## Change

Set `relativeTopStory = 0` whenever an explicit `height` is applied (in the Modify commands together with the corresponding mask bit). Callers who want story-linked elements keep using the linked tool default — creating **without** `height` is unchanged.

## Testing (live against AC28, Win, story grid UG −3.0 / EG 0.0 / OG 3.0)

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `CreateColumns` `height: 2.0` | bbox zMax 2.65 (link wins) | ✅ zMax 2.0 |
| `CreateColumns` without `height` | zMax 2.65 (template default) | ✅ zMax 2.65 — unchanged |
| `ModifyColumns` `height: 1.5` | no effect on linked column | ✅ zMax 1.5 |
| `CreateWalls` `height: 2.2` | template-dependent | ✅ zMax 2.2 |
| `ModifyWalls` `height: 1.8` | template-dependent | ✅ zMax 1.8 |

title: Let Column/Slab/Object/Lamp/Beam/Stair/Roof/Morph creation take an explicit floorIndex
body:
## Summary

Several element-creation commands derived the new element's floor purely by guessing from a Z/level coordinate (`GetFloorIndexAndOffset`), with no way to pin the floor explicitly. A Z value near a story boundary could land on the wrong floor, and there was no way to force a specific one — the same class of bug already fixed for `CreateMeshes`/`CreateTexts`.

This adds an optional `floorIndex` input to the commands that were still missing it.

## What changed

- Added a shared helper, `ResolveFloorIndexAndOffset` (`CommandBase.hpp`/`.cpp`): identical to the existing Z-guess when no `floorIndex` is given, but an explicit `floorIndex` picks the story directly. The offset is still computed from the given Z (via `GetZPos`), so the element's **absolute 3D position is preserved exactly** — only which floor-plan it's grouped under changes.
- Applied it to:
  - `CreateColumns`
  - `CreateSlabs`
  - `CreateObjects` / `CreateLamps` (share `SetLibraryPartElementParameters`)
  - `CreateBeams`
  - `CreateStairs`
  - `ApplyRoofDetails` — shared with the existing modify-roof command, so modifying an existing roof's level also benefits, even though `CreateRoofs` itself is a separate pre-existing no-op (multi-plane pivot-edge setup was never implemented) unrelated to this change.
- `CreateMorphs` got its own fix: it never derived `header.floorInd` from position at all — it silently used whatever `ACAPI_Element_GetDefaults` defaulted to, regardless of the requested position. Now computed via the same helper, while its transform matrix's absolute Z placement (already correct) is left untouched.

## Not affected

- `CreateWalls` already had `floorIndex` support.
- `CreateWindows` / `CreateDoors` / `CreateOpenings` never had this bug: they're positioned relative to a host element (`ownerWallId` / `ownerElementId`), with no absolute Z to guess a floor from.

## Testing

Compiled cleanly on AC25/26/27/29.

Live-verified on AC29 and AC25 with a disposable test script: for Column, Slab, Beam, Stair, Morph, and Object, created one instance at a Z that would naturally guess floor B, both with no `floorIndex` (confirms the guess fallback still works) and with an explicit `floorIndex=A` that contradicts the guess (confirms the override wins) — read back via `GetDetailsOfElements`. 12/12 checks passed on AC29, 10/10 on AC25 (AC25's project incidentally has a basement story, so this also exercised a negative floor index).

Specifically double-checked that the fix changes the floor *assignment* and not the element's real position: creating a Column with `floorIndex=-1` at `z=0.5` (which would guess floor `0`) came back as:

```json
{
  "floorIndex": -1,
  "details": {
    "zCoordinate": 0.5,
    "bottomOffset": 3.3
  }
}
```

i.e. `floorIndex` reflects the override, `zCoordinate` stays exactly as requested (not snapped to floor `-1`'s own base level of `-2.8`), and `bottomOffset` is correctly back-computed (`0.5 - (-2.8) = 3.3`).
